newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to display treaty that ceded HK to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to display treaty that ceded HK to Britain.

text.p: Taipei will put on public display the 1842 Sino-British treaty that ceded Hong Kong to Britain, Taiwan's foreign minister said on Tuesday.

The Chinese version of the Treaty of Nanking, signed by Qing dynasty rulers on August 29, 1842, would be unveiled at a Taiwan museum before Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, John Chang told the state-run Central News Agency.
"The foreign ministry will let the outside world see the actual Treaty of Nanking so as to foster meaningful discussions," Chang was quoted as saying.

The Qing dynasty was toppled in 1911 and replaced by China's first modern government, the Nationalist-led Republic of China, which itself fell to Chinese communist troops in 1949 and fled into exile on Taiwan.
The treaty was brought to Taiwan by the Nationalists and has been held on the island.
Chang did not say why Taipei wanted to coordinate the display with Hong Kong's historic handover.
Taiwan has not challenged China's right to take back Hong Kong, a handover negotiated between Beijing and London in 1984.
The English version of the treaty is kept in London.
